key_insight: A total-pressure formulation enables locking-free poroelastic optimal control with first-order error bounds uniform as the Lamé parameter increases.
engineering_relevance: The method supports source-control design in nearly incompressible porous materials while tracking displacement and fluid pressure and enforcing control limits.
method: Use a mechanical Schur complement to establish zero-storage well-posedness for each fixed finite Lamé parameter.
Discretize state and adjoint with conforming finite elements and dG(0) time stepping.
Represent box-constrained source controls as piecewise constants.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments confirm predicted convergence rates, examine Lamé-parameter and storage dependence, and demonstrate localized pressure control with active bounds.
watch_item: The first-order error estimates require the stated regularity assumptions and a positive storage lower bound; zero-storage well-posedness does not establish uniform zero-storage error bounds.
paper_title: Locking-free numerical methods for poroelasticity optimal control problems with minimal regularities
